conversations.summary: Maya found flights for 16–23 May and wants to book the Alfama apartment by Friday.
brief: Maya wants to book Casa Azul in Alfama for 16–23 May, and asks you to confirm.
Book by Friday: the host says someone else asked about those dates.
Flights for the week of 16 May are cheap; her draft itinerary is attached.
conversations.reply: Perfect, that works for me! I'll book the apartment tonight and send you the details. 🎉

messages.subject: Lisbon in May?
messages.text:
Hi Alex,

Remember how we said we'd finally do Lisbon? I looked at flights and the week of 16 May is surprisingly cheap.

Are you in?

Maya

I'm so in. Let's do it.

Should we stay in Alfama? I'd love to be able to walk everywhere.

Alex

Alfama it is. I found a small apartment with a terrace (Casa Azul). The host, Tomás, says it's free 16–23 May.

Shall I book it?

It looks lovely! Let me check that week with work and I'll get back to you by tomorrow.

Alex

Quick nudge: Tomás says someone else asked about those dates, so we should book by Friday.

I attached the itinerary I've sketched so far. Tell me what you think!

M.

conversations.summary: Issue 48: one inbox for many accounts, shortcuts as a language, small tools.

messages.subject: Fewer tabs, better afternoons
messages.text: The Slow Web, Issue 48. This week: why a single, quiet inbox beats five noisy ones, a short essay on keyboard shortcuts as a kind of fluency, and three small tools that do one thing well.
messages.html:
The Slow Web · Issue 48
Fewer tabs, better afternoons
This week: why a single, quiet inbox beats five noisy ones, a short essay on keyboard shortcuts as a kind of fluency, and three small tools that do one thing well.
1. One inbox, many accounts
Reading everything in one place, with a quiet color for each account, removes a surprising amount of friction.
2. Shortcuts are a language
Learn three a week. By spring you will not reach for the mouse.
3. Small tools
A timer, a notebook, and a calendar that stays out of the way.
Read the full issue
